coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 5
record.summary: Planned residential highrise tower on the Potrero Power Station masterplan, up to 220 ft; the developer's 2026 Development Agreement amendment request would let the entire block become PDR/lab space (up to a 'small data center') instead, with no construction start found to date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram via multi-point real-street georeferencing (see digitization_method), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes (as already found for the UCSF/Sophie Maxwell area -- see digitization_method). Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade, and treat the block's applicability itself as somewhat more provisional than Mission Rock's or Pier 70's equivalent entries. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 via GDAL GCP/TPS georeferencing -- see digitization_method. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (third pass) in a single consistent pixel-detection pass across the whole block layout -- see digitization_method. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (fourth pass) after fixing a mis-measured GCP -- see digitization_method.
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
notes.regulatory_context: Figure 6.2.3 shows Block 5 (marked '5*', a potential district parking garage/grocery store site, like Block 1) with an 85 ft base and a 220 ft max upper height, with a '111' MAX' sub-callout -- a notably tall potential tower for this site. Program and construction status not independently confirmed by any source found beyond this figure.

facts.value: Residential, Institutional, Retail and Non-Retail Sales/Services uses permitted, plus limited PDR uses at the lowest floors (e.g. Light Manufacturing, Arts Activities, Business Services); Laboratory and Life Science uses Not Permitted under the adopted D4D final Table 3.1.1 -- the 2026 proposed DA amendment would add full-PDR flexibility (see milestones)

85 ft base with a 220 ft max upper tower, and a distinct 111 ft max callout on part of the block, per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3; the D4D's height-category text separately places Block 5 in a 'Highrise towers' category of 181-240 ft
One of three blocks (with 1 and 13) eligible to host the project's single permitted district parking garage (max 90 ft, with a publicly accessible rooftop sports field)
Not listed among the six Phase 1 blocks (2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15) named in the 2024 annual compliance report

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement that first names Block 5 as a development block under the adopted Design for Development's Land Use Table; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 5; it is not one of the six buildings named in the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list (Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15), and no later-phase design review approval was found either.

The Development Agreement amendment described in the Chronicle (July 2026) was pending Planning Commission/Board of Supervisors action as of this dossier's last-verified date; recorded here as a proposal, not an adopted change.
No phase-specific schedule found for Block 5; the added expected-completion milestone therefore uses only the whole-project buildout target (2035, SocketSite Oct 2020), not a block-specific date.
